correctness.rationale: The quotient-projectivization and degree conventions agree with Denisi–Höring. Their graded-ring identification transfers the calculation to the elementary transform F. Independently, a section of Sym^m T_M is meromorphic in Sym^m F with poles of order at most m on C_-; if the order k is positive, its leading term lies in Sym^m(F|C_-) tensor L^k, which has a filtration by negative-degree line bundles and no sections. This removes the poles. Twisting the symmetric-power filtration of F by -C_- gives quotients O(jC_+-C_-). For j=0 the fibre degree is -1 and all cohomology vanishes; for 1≤j≤m the direct image is the sum of L^{-i}, 1≤i≤j, with no higher image. Riemann–Roch gives id sections and zero H^1 per summand. The twisted H^1 consequently vanishes, so restriction to C_- adds exactly one section from Sym^m F_2, also for m=0. Summing yields the claimed series and leading coefficient d/6. The projective-bundle formula yields ζ^3=c_1(T_M)^2-c_2(T_M)=0 using the two disjoint sections of self-intersections ±d and the elliptic base. The frozen integer checker only tests finite arithmetic identities, not the geometry; it was inspected, not executed.
